check: ADR-0032 §8 batch E-check (2026-09-21): does the installed dsh ACP bridge put command exit codes into tool_call_update.rawOutput (or any other structurally parseable field)?
method: static, zero-token, zero-model: read-only source inspection of the locally installed dsh packages; no dispatch, no credentials

searched.target: protocol schema (does ToolCallUpdate even have rawOutput?)
where exit codes are rendered into tool-result text

findings: VERIFIED-NEGATIVE (rawOutput): the ACP bridge's toolResultUpdate (dsh-acp lib/index.js) emits sessionUpdate "tool_call_update" with exactly { toolCallId, status, content } — it does NOT populate rawOutput, even though @agentclientprotocol/sdk's schema declares an optional rawOutput?: unknown field (types.gen.d.ts). Conclusion: the field exists in the protocol but this dsh version leaves it unset.

VERIFIED (text markers only): command exit codes reach the tool result only as free-form text. dsh-tool-pwsh/dsh-tool-bash renderPwshResult appends a marker line '[exit code: N]' ONLY for non-zero exits (a clean exit 0 produces no marker at all); the process outcome detail string 'exit code: N' goes to the jobs registry, not to the ACP wire.

VERIFIED (content conversion is lossy): the bridge converts tool-result content blocks via assistantBlockToAcp, which passes ONLY text and image block types; every other structured block type is dropped (returns undefined). No structured exit-code block survives onto tool_call_update.

VERIFIED (WAO-side): deepSeekAcp.js handleToolCallUpdate reads update.content and runs extractExitCode (a line-anchored regex matching lines of the form 'exit code: N' / 'exitcode=N'). Two independent breaks: (a) the rendered marker is '[exit code: N]' which starts with '[' so the line-anchored regex never matches; (b) contentText() only joins blocks of literal type 'text', while the bridge emits '{type:"content", content:{type:"text",...}}' wrappers, so even the text body is not extracted. Additionally the scorecard inference channel (withInferredCommandExitCode matching command.toolCallId against tool_result.tool) cannot fire: the bridge's toolResultEvent uses the tool NAME as the correlation key, not the toolCallId.

CONSISTENT with the real delta record: runs/reliability-summary.json deepseek_acp_deltadrill shows commandsPassed 'failed (exitCode!=0): node --version (exitCode=undefined)' — the command ran, no exit code was extractable.
conclusion: CANNOT support command exit-code evidence today: tool_call_update.rawOutput is NOT populated by dsh-acp 0.1.5-rc.2, and no other structurally parseable exit-code field exists on that notification. Exit codes surface only as free-form '[exit code: N]' text markers for non-zero exits (exit 0 leaves no trace). This grounds the honest declaration reportsCommandExitCode=false on DeepSeekAcpBackend and the not-applicable treatment of commandsPassed-type checks (ADR-0032 §8).
flipConditions: upstream populates tool_call_update.rawOutput (or another structured field) with the exit code, AND
WAO wires that field in deepSeekAcp.js with real-dispatch evidence (a phase-style probe) — declaration flips only with verified evidence, per the supportsSessionReuse/reportsTokenUsage precedent
notCovered: the client terminal API path (task brief notes ACP exit codes live only there) was not inspected in this check — no WAO code path consumes it today, and the bridge-side verdict above is already conclusive for the declaration
dsh versions other than 0.1.5-rc.2 (re-run this static check after any dsh upgrade; it is zero-token)
